intentions.title: Give every product surface (documents, media DAM, future surfaces) a single unified relevance pipeline: parse → expand synonyms → retrieve → recover-from-zero-hits → highlight
intentions.evidence: QueryPipeline.search/4 dispatches on `surface` tag through one parse→expand→retrieve→recover→highlight chain; DocumentsRetriever implements the Barkpark.Search.Retriever behaviour so Postgres and future non-Postgres engines (Indx) share the same contract; Retrievers.ex is the registry; SurfaceConfigs.get/2 supplies per-surface tuning (searchable_fields, typo_policy, zero_hit_strategy, low_hit_threshold) so each surface tunes ranking without forking the pipeline code.

intentions.title: Make search self-improving: turn raw query events into crystallized analytics, synonym suggestions, and golden-query regression scoring so search quality gets measurably better over time
intentions.evidence: Intelligence.record/6 + Event schema capture every query; Crystallizer.crystallize_due/1 rolls raw events into day/week/month Crystal aggregates with self-healing backfill (@backfill_days) for missed cron/Oban runs; MergePattern detects candidate synonym pairs from co-occurring reformulations; GoldenEval.run/3 scores retrieval (MRR, NDCG@10, zero-hit-rate) against JSONL fixtures and GoldenEval.compare/2 fails a regression check; Synonyms module turns detected patterns (or manual entries) into query-time expansion via search_terms/3.

intentions.title: Never let search analytics/telemetry break or slow down the actual search request
intentions.evidence: Intelligence.record/6 and record_interaction/4 wrap every path in rescue/catch and always return :skipped rather than raising — moduledoc states 'analytics must not break search'; DocumentsRetriever bounds ranking cost via @default_ranking_pool_size (500) so a broad query doesn't pay full ts_rank/similarity cost on the whole corpus.

intentions.title: Fail closed on cross-tenant/cross-owner data exposure in full-text search results
intentions.evidence: DocumentsRetriever.search/4 applies scope_to_workspace_or_global and scope_to_owner unconditionally on every query; comments explain a nil caller_context restricts to owner_id IS NULL only (never another owner's rows) — 'a no-op solely for non-owner_scoped types, never a window onto another owner's rows'; QueryPipeline comment: a non-Postgres engine without workspace_id in opts falls back to the scoped Postgres retriever rather than risk a cross-workspace bypass.

intentions.title: Treat every unauthenticated/anonymous search input as hostile: sanitize, bound, and cap before it touches the database or gets persisted as analytics
intentions.evidence: Sanitizer rejects invalid UTF-8, non-binary params, spam/punctuation-only/control-char/profanity queries, and enforces length bounds before storage ('Rejected queries are never stored verbatim'); DocumentsRetriever clamps limit (max 200) and offset (max 100_000) to stop unbounded LIMIT/OFFSET abuse as 'a free DoS amplifier on public browse'; SurfaceConfigs caps its ETS config cache at 512 entries with clear-on-full eviction so an attacker can't grow it unbounded via arbitrary scope strings.

intentions.title: Let each surface/scope tune its own ranking behavior (field weights, typo tolerance, zero-hit strategy) without code forks, cached for hot-path performance
intentions.evidence: SurfaceConfigs stores per-{surface,scope} tuning in a bounded ETS cache with 60s TTL (chosen over :persistent_term specifically to avoid BEAM-wide global GC per key, per its moduledoc); ships @default_documents and @default_media config maps (searchable_fields with weights, typo_policy thresholds, zero_hit_strategy, low_hit_threshold, highlight_fields) that SurfaceConfig Ecto rows can override.

intentions.title: Support operator-manageable synonym/correction rules (manual or auto-detected) that transparently expand and relabel search results
intentions.evidence: Synonyms.create/3, .list/2, .delete/3 provide CRUD over Synonym rows with `kind` (one_way vs alt_correction) and `source` (manual vs auto); search_terms/3 expands a raw query with synonym targets; QueryPipeline.expand_synonyms/3 also surfaces `corrected_to` so the UI can show 'Showing results for …'; MergePattern + Crystallizer auto-detect candidate synonyms from real query reformulation behavior.
